title: of Goods and Services
status: draft: written 18 Nov 2026 offline for Grade 8 Pre-Technical Studies; not yet checked by a Pre-Technical Studies teacher; safety lines marked SAFETY in the library to confirm first; not loaded by the live tutor

skills.key_step: The learner explains why marketing matters (finds and keeps customers, informs them, increases sales), names sources of market information (customers, surveys, competitors, the media, trade fairs), the factors in choosing a market (demand, ability to pay, location and access, competition, cost), suitable markets for goods and services, and marketing tools (posters, signboards, social media, radio, samples, word of mouth).

floor.question: What does a sales book show?
floor.answer: What was sold and for how much

steps: Pick a tool and say why.
contexts: a new bakery in the market
a youth group selling crafts online

board.do: Write: "a new bakery near a school".

board.say: Who are the customers, and how will the bakery reach them?

board.do: Wait for the learner to name learners and parents; a poster or social media.

listen_for: Only takes the money at the till
misconceptions.repair: Trace how a customer hears of a new shop (poster, friend, radio) before buying: that is marketing.

listen_for: Make what the owner likes best
misconceptions.ask: What is the most reliable way for a new bakery to find out what customers want?
misconceptions.repair: Run a short class survey on snacks; compare the result with one person's guess.

misconceptions.ask: Which factor matters most when choosing where to sell school uniforms?
misconceptions.repair: List what a market needs: customers who want the goods and can pay, access, competition, cost of reaching it.

misconceptions.ask: Which is a marketing tool a small shop can use?
misconceptions.repair: Sort shop items into equipment (till, shelves) and marketing tools (posters, signboards, social media pages, radio adverts, samples).

checks.question: Name a source of market information.
